title: Russian Missile Flattens Ukrainian Apartment Block, Killing 19 Including Five Children
excerpt: President Zelensky called the October 7 strike on Pryluky — which fell on Vladimir Putin's 74th birthday — one of the most vile of the nearly five-year war.
body:
• A Russian missile struck a five-story apartment building in Pryluky, in Ukraine’s Chernihiv region, at about 6:30 a.m. on October 7, collapsing half the block as residents slept; 19 people were killed, including five children — three of them just one year old.
  • President Volodymyr Zelensky called it “one of the most vile strikes” of the nearly five-year war, suggesting the destroyed block was a birthday “gift” for Vladimir Putin, who turned 74 the same day.
  • The strike was part of a wider barrage of about 70 missiles — many of them ballistic — plus dozens of drones across Ukraine; at least 26 people were killed nationwide, with deaths also reported in Kyiv, Kremenchuk and Oleksandriya.
  • Moscow did not acknowledge the Pryluky strike, saying its “massive strike” targeted military industries; Ukraine said it retaliated by hitting oil facilities and a training ground in Russia’s Perm, Samara and Astrakhan regions.

A town wakes to rubble

The missile hit the ordinary five-story apartment building in Pryluky, east of Kyiv, in the early morning as families slept. The blast reduced half of the block to a smoking pile of charred concrete and twisted metal. Regional governor Viacheslav Chaus told national television that 13 people were dead, four of them children, and more than 50 injured — and the toll kept rising as rescue crews worked through the debris. The State Emergency Service later put the local toll at 19 killed, including five children, with at least 50 wounded, seven of them children. Fifteen people, including one child, were pulled out alive.

https://x.com/RpsAgainstTrump/status/2107918394649370866

Three of the dead children were just 12 months old — named by Zelensky as Oleksandr, Kyrylo and Serhii. An eight-year-old boy, Maxsym, was also killed, and a fifth child’s body was recovered from the rubble in the evening. One boy, Sasha, died alongside his mother Kateryna and grandmother Viktoriia; only his elder sister Olha survived.

“We were at home, sleeping. Our windows blew out. Thank God, we covered the child with our bodies.”

— Olena Sayun, a Pryluky resident, quoted by AFP

“A deliberate choice of terror”

President Zelensky accused Russia of knowingly striking civilian life. “The continued use of missiles against Ukraine, against our people, our children, is an absolutely deliberate choice of terror,” he said. He added that the attack was intended to inflict pain — and noted its timing on Putin’s 74th birthday.

The barrage was not confined to one town. Zelensky said infrastructure in Kyiv and 12 regions was attacked. In the capital, two people were killed in a fire at a garage cooperative in the Darnytskyi district; residents sheltered in subway stations as air raid sirens wailed. Two people were killed in Kremenchuk, two in Oleksandriya, and apartment buildings were damaged in Dnipro and Zaporizhzhia. Power cuts plunged parts of Kyiv into darkness, with traffic disrupted and water cuts on the capital’s right bank.

The air war, in numbers

Ukraine’s air force said Russia launched at least 50 missiles and 130 drones overnight against several regions, and that it had intercepted five ballistic missiles, 39 cruise missiles and more than 100 drones. Zelensky said ballistic missiles remained “the greatest challenge” and that new air defenses were essential. Ukraine has been struggling to down fast-moving jet-powered drones as well as ballistic missiles that are harder to intercept.

Moscow did not acknowledge the attack on Pryluky but stated its “massive strike” was aimed at military industries in Kyiv and other locations.

Retaliation and a grim winter ahead

Ukraine struck back. Zelensky said Ukraine’s “just responses” hit two oil facilities and a training ground in Russia’s Perm, Samara and Astrakhan regions, as well as targets in the Black Sea. In the Russia-occupied part of Ukraine’s Kherson region, two people, including a teenage girl, were killed in a drone strike, according to the Moscow-backed head of the region — a reminder that civilian casualties are mounting on both sides as Ukraine steps up long-range attacks on targets it says are vital to Russia’s war effort.

Kyiv’s mayor warned last week that the capital should be on a war footing as winter approaches, with repeated strikes on bridges and energy infrastructure. After Pryluky, that warning reads less like preparation and more like a description of the present.
